pages.text: "Sweet! One more, please." Yuki chewed dried persimmons on the quilt. Their fingertips were sticky. Grandma came with a toothbrush, wearing gray layered clothes.
"I don't want to brush. I want to lie under the quilt!" Yuki shook their head and slipped inside. The toothbrush stayed where it was.
In the middle of the night, Yuki woke. Something tickled between their teeth. Pushing with the tongue found a soft persimmon piece stuck there. "What's in my mouth?"
Grandma came with a lamp. "Say ah." She removed the piece from between the teeth. "The sweet juice stayed behind."
"Little round bugs that love sweet juice roll around there." Yuki could almost see them tumbling and grinning between the teeth. "I'll chase them away!"
"They can't stay when bubbles rush in." Grandma offered the brush. Yuki jumped up, gripped it, and squeezed on some toothpaste.
Up went the brush, then down! White foam puffed around Yuki's mouth. The round bugs were pushed out in a rush of bubbles. "After Something Sweet, Brush, Brush!"
Yuki rinsed and opened wide. Smooth teeth showed; the tickle was gone. Brown dog Momo, asleep at their feet, tapped the floor with their tail.

The next day, Yuki took the brush right after the persimmon. Fixing the scarf knot, Yuki counted clearly. "One, right after sweets! Two, again before the lamp goes out! Three, brush between every tooth!"
On Grandma's lap, Yuki opened wide to show their mouth. She gently stroked their back. Brushing right after sweets stopped the tickling. "After Something Sweet, Brush, Brush!"
